newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM precious metals slip, palladium off lows.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM precious metals slip, palladium off lows.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metal futures settled lower across the board on Thursday, following sharp losses in bullion prices and the yen's firmer tendency against the dollar, traders said.
Palladium futures ended down, but off early lows.

Despite a media report that Russia expects palladium supplies to Japan to resume in March, Japanese traders said there had been no word yet from the Russian platinum group export agency (Almaz) on when Japan-Russia contract talks will be held. "Uncertainty over prospects for Russia's resumption of exports sidelined Japanese traders," one trader said.
Palladium futures ranged from eight yen to 13 yen per gram lower. Most-active benchmark February was off 12 yen at 585 yen after slipping to 577 yen earlier in the day.

Japanese traders said Russia is likely to resume sales of platinum group metals in the spot market sometime soon after the overhaul of the Russian government was announced, but they were sure that there will be no shipments in March, and April shipments were also in doubt.
In palladium futures, short-covering by private investors was countered by long-liquidation. In platinum futures, some bargain-hunting partly offset price losses.
